subject: GPU pool capacity squeeze — customer incident & exec sync
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com
Cc: support_ops@acme-corp.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike — reserved throughput not met

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing end-user latency jump and a 5xx error spike around 14:50 UTC for our prod tenant. This is on our reserved capacity pool (pool id 78). Our telemetry shows sustained queueing and token throughput well below our committed rate despite the pool showing all nodes as healthy. Attached is a short metric snapshot and a sample request trace.

Impact: several customers report timeouts in checkout flows (high priority). We are already in severity 2 for our internal ops. Please advise immediate mitigation and a timeline to restore committed throughput. Also confirm whether any customer data left our VPC during mitigations.

- Lena
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Corp
lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com

Attachments: acme_error_metric_snapshot.png, acme_request_sample.log

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — reserved throughput not met

Thanks for the alert, Lena — sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as priority. Quick summary of immediate actions we are initiating now:

- Triggering emergency spill routing to a warm hosted pool (read-only routing) to reduce queueing while preserving tenant isolation.
- Increasing reserved pool target by adding 2 standby GPU nodes from our reserve (expected in ~12–18 minutes).
- Short-term priority queuing for checkout-related routes only (to protect checkout traffic).
- Capturing KV cache state and request traces; we will not move any customer data outside your VPC unless you approve failover.

Could you confirm whether we have permission to route a subset of requests to hosted warm nodes for up to 2 hours as a stopgap? If not, we’ll proceed with capacity add + throttling only.

I attached a mutual action plan (MAP_v1.3.pdf) with the step sequence and owners. We'll follow up with a short exec note once we have confirmed throughput metrics.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v1.3.pdf

On Fri, Apr 9, 2027 at 15:02 Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Hi Jasmine,
> 
> We started seeing end-user latency jump and a 5xx error spike around 14:50 UTC for our prod tenant...

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike — reserved throughput not met

Team — forwarding the escalation from Acme (see attached metrics). TL;DR: reserved pool 78 is delivering ~60% of committed throughput under the current workload; queue depth climbing and checkout route seeing 500s. Customer is asking for ETA and confirmation no data leaves VPC.

Prelim hypothesis (from infra logs):
- One of the pool autoscale controllers failed to apply the recent scaling policy change (regression introduced in delivery job INFRA-8727).
- A sudden rollout on the customer's side produced a traffic shape with small, high-concurrency requests that reduced batching efficiency and increased per-token overhead.

Immediate asks:
1) Need exec-level sync and decision on temporary cross-tenant spill to hosted warm nodes (customer approval requested).
2) Approve emergency +2 GPU standby add to pool 78 and bump priority for reprovisioning (we estimate ~15 mins to effective capacity once nodes join).
3) Finance/CS guidance on single-day credit if SLA breached.
4) Neha — can you prepare a 1-page incident brief for execs (impact, ETA, mitigation, credit ask)?

I'll coordinate the customer comms; need leadership direction on the hosted spill and credit thresholds so I can provide definitive answers to Lena.

Thanks,
-Jasmine

On Fri, Apr 9, 2027 15:28 Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the alert, Lena — sorry for the disruption...

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 17:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike — reserved throughput not met

Thanks for the quick triage, Jasmine. Approve the +2 GPU standby add and immediate priority to reprovisioning. Approve hosted spill for up to 1 hour while we verify capacity, provided we document the exact request routing subset and get written permission from Acme (Lena) — please capture that approval in the MAP.

Neha — please draft the one-pager and include a recommended credit range for a partial SLA miss (I suggest 10–20% on impacted hours as a starting point).

Also, schedule a 30-minute exec sync at 08:30 PT tomorrow with Customer Success, Platform, and Sales leadership (I will join). We’ll need: current throughput numbers, exact error rates, and a short rollback/rollback trigger checklist.

— Vivek
VP, Product & Operations
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Apr 9, 2027 17:05 Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding the escalation from Acme...

Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — reserved throughput not met

Thanks Jasmine — we approve routing up to 30% of checkout traffic to your hosted warm nodes for up to 60 minutes while you increase capacity. Please ensure headers/traces preserve tenant id and do not leave PII outside our VPC.

We need an ETA for restored committed throughput and a next-step cadence. Please confirm the exec sync time and who will join from product/infra.

-Lena
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Corp
